QA Summary - 31 August 2026

Verdict: FAILED - Confirmed functional defect

Item Result
Scope Edit Collection / Rename from the three-dot menu
Environment User-confirmed Android real-device test; authenticated Tester Account 1; owned unpublished collection
Expected Rename opens a clear edit flow, saves the changed name, and the renamed collection remains visible after refresh.
Actual Selecting Rename from the three-dot menu fails to continue through a usable rename flow.
Impact An owner cannot reliably rename an unpublished collection through the exposed menu.
Evidence Raw attachment is embedded below.

Reproduction Steps

# Action Expected result Actual result Status
1 Log in and open an owned unpublished collection. Collection detail opens. Opened. Pass
2 Open the three-dot menu. Owner actions are visible. Menu shown. Pass
3 Select Rename/Edit. Edit screen or name form opens. Flow fails; no reliable rename continuation. Fail
4 Return to the collection list. Existing collection data remains intact. No destructive mutation performed. Pass

Test Method Coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Owner opens an unpublished collection and invokes Rename through the exposed three-dot menu. Fail
Gray-box Authenticated owner state and unpublished collection are available, but the UI handoff does not complete. Fail
White-box Reviewed menu-to-edit routing, delayed navigation, edit payload, and error handling. Defect candidate supports runtime result

Confusion Matrix

Actual condition / Test decision Feature accepted Feature rejected
Valid owner rename action 0 TP 1 FN
Invalid/non-owner action Not executed Not executed

Code Review

Area Observation Risk
Three-dot action routing The legacy collection action closes its sheet and delays navigation to CollectionEdit. Handoff can fail silently.
Error visibility Navigation is wrapped in an empty catch block. Runtime routing errors are suppressed.
Edit persistence The edit screen prepares the update request and cache refresh path. The entry flow, not the intended update contract, is the observed failure point.
Active collection model Current profile collections use a newer published-folder model while the menu path remains legacy collection-post code. Flow ownership/route contract is ambiguous.

Developer Follow-up

  1. Define the canonical owner flow for unpublished collections: current collection model versus legacy collection-post screens.
  2. Make Rename route deterministically from the three-dot menu and surface routing/request errors.
  3. Add a real-device regression test: three-dot menu -> Rename -> Save -> refresh/relaunch verification.

Evidence

QA Summary - 31 August 2026

Verdict: FAILED - Confirmed functional defect

Item Result
Scope Delete Collection from the three-dot menu
Environment User-confirmed Android real-device test; authenticated Tester Account 1; owned unpublished collection
Expected Delete opens a clear confirmation, removes the selected collection only after confirmation, and returns to the collection list.
Actual Selecting Delete from the three-dot menu fails to continue through a usable delete flow.
Impact An owner cannot reliably remove an unpublished collection through the exposed menu.
Safety No unintended collection deletion was performed.
Evidence Raw attachment is embedded below.

Reproduction Steps

# Action Expected result Actual result Status
1 Log in and open an owned unpublished collection. Collection detail opens. Opened. Pass
2 Open the three-dot menu. Owner actions are visible. Menu shown. Pass
3 Select Delete. Confirmation dialog opens before any deletion. Flow fails; no reliable delete continuation. Fail
4 Return to the collection list. Original collection remains because deletion was not confirmed. Preserved. Pass

Test Method Coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Owner invokes Delete from the exposed three-dot menu. Fail
Gray-box Authenticated owner and unpublished collection state are available, but UI handoff does not complete. Fail
White-box Reviewed delayed delete-modal trigger, delete request, cache refresh, and error handling. Defect candidate supports runtime result

Confusion Matrix

Actual condition / Test decision Feature accepted Feature rejected
Valid owner delete action 0 TP 1 FN
Cancel/invalid/non-owner action Not executed Not executed

Code Review

Area Observation Risk
Three-dot delete routing The legacy action closes the sheet, then delays opening the confirmation modal. Modal handoff can fail silently.
Error visibility The modal-open path is wrapped in an empty catch block. Runtime action failures are hidden.
Delete contract The intended service deletes by collection slug, clears cache, refreshes Profile, and shows an error alert on request failure. The observed failure occurs before safe confirmation/deletion.
Active collection model Current profile collections use a newer published-folder model while the menu path remains legacy collection-post code. Flow ownership/route contract is ambiguous.

Developer Follow-up

  1. Define the canonical delete flow for unpublished collections.
  2. Make the three-dot Delete action open a deterministic confirmation dialog; do not swallow handoff errors.
  3. Add a real-device regression test: three-dot menu -> Delete -> Cancel -> Delete -> Confirm -> refresh/relaunch verification.
